title: Speculative decode orchestration: candidate scoring, acceptance thresholds, and graceful fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime orchestration layer for speculative decoding that can (a) route a request to multiple candidate model variants for prefill and decode, (b) score candidate outputs quickly in-kernel using lightweight acceptance heuristics, and (c) execute fast graceful fallback to baseline model variants when acceptance thresholds are not met or when kernel/hardware incompatibilities are detected. Scope includes kernel selection hooks, attention-optimization flags for short vs long-context candidates, prefill/decode scheduling policies, and visible acceptance metrics for rollouts.

Motivation: Current single-variant decode cannot leverage cheap smaller models for early tokens then switch to larger models on failure without complex orchestration on the control plane. Speculative decoding reduces average latency and GPU cost for common inputs, but requires careful runtime support to avoid quality regressions and SLO violations. This ticket implements the runtime primitives and rollout controls necessary for safe production adoption.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can concurrently schedule a prefill on a low-cost candidate and a speculative decode on a high-capacity candidate and reconcile outputs deterministically
Lightweight acceptance scorer returns a boolean within 1.5ms median for 2048-sequence requests (measured on runtime infra)
Fallback engages automatically when acceptance_rate < 0.9 or when candidate kernel selection fails; fallbacks must not increase median P95 latency by >5% for baseline traffic
End-to-end tests covering race conditions, KV-cache validity across speculative handoffs, and multi-variant quantization compatibility
Instrumented dashboards showing acceptance_rate, candidate_latency_delta, decode_success_rate, and fallback_count per model-route
technical_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Acceptance scorer will use a hybrid approach: fast in-GPU heuristics (token overlap, prefix-match ratios) implemented as a CUDA kernel path where possible, with a contingency CPU-side validator for edge cases. 2) Kernel selection should consider attention strategy (sparse/flash attention) and KV cache layout; cheaper candidates use quantized kernels that favor lower memory but must expose a compatible cache format for handoff. 3) Prefill scheduling: attempt prefill on candidate A (cheap) and pre-allocate KV regions for candidate B (expensive) only if A's prefill confidence falls below a threshold to reduce wasted GPU cycles. 4) Fallback policy: prefer model-variant fallback over region fallback to preserve latency SLOs.

Trade-offs: implementing full in-GPU acceptance kernels increases runtime complexity but reduces cross-device sync cost. CPU-based scoring is simpler to iterate on but risks added latency for high-QPS routes. We will prototype both and gate the in-kernel path behind a rollout flag.
implementation_plan:
1) Runtime API extension: add speculative_candidates array to decode request payload, including candidate_priority and kernel_hint. 2) Kernel adapters: introduce speculative_accept kqueue and lightweight scorer kernel; add kernel selection hooks that expose attention-mode compatibility. 3) Prefill/decode scheduler: extend scheduler to allow paired prefill+decode reservations and a fast preemption path. 4) Metrics: add acceptance_rate, candidate_latency_delta_ms, fallback_count, kv_handshake_errors to telemetry. 5) E2E tests and load tests: create scenario suites in the ci-perf job to validate throughput and P95 under mixed traffic.

Milestones: Week 1: API + scheduler prototype; Week 2: in-GPU scorer POC + kernel adapters; Week 3: integration, test harness, and canary rollout; Week 4: monitor and iterate on thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KV cache incompatibility between quantized candidate and full-precision model could corrupt context. Mitigation: handshake protocol that refuses speculative handoff if cache layouts mismatch; add automated cache-compatibility checks during model onboarding.

Risk: Acceptance scorer false positives leading to degraded output quality. Mitigation: keep canary traffic at 1-2% with human-in-loop QA for new heuristics; add quality-based regression alerting tied to prompt-suite evaluations.
Risk: Scheduler fragmentation causing lower overall throughput. Mitigation: implement pooling and bin-packing heuristics; add autoscale signals tuned for speculative traffic patterns.
testing_plan: Unit tests for acceptance scorer kernel (CUDA and CPU fallback), integration tests that validate KV integrity across speculative handoffs, and stress tests to measure median and P95 latency under 1000 rps. Add mutation tests where acceptance thresholds are varied to measure impact on quality metrics. Schedule a 2-week canary with 1-5% traffic routed to speculative path and daily evaluation against a fixed prompt set.
